verdict.rationale: Honeybadger ships its own non-interactive automation surfaces: a CLI with `honeybadger deploy` and `honeybadger exec`, which wraps a command and reports a non-zero exit, plus REST APIs for deploy notification, source-map upload, error reporting and fault queries. These can run headlessly in pipelines, but the CLI is documented as part of the Ruby gem and no CI-specific guidance is shown. missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline documentation, a language-agnostic standalone CLI, an OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: honeybadger exec — Execute a command. If the exit status is not 0, report the result to Honeybadger
Use this endpoint to notify Honeybadger when a deploy occurs.
Use the Source Map Upload API to upload your source maps to Honeybadger.
The Capistrano integration for tracking deployments is really handy.
